briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Google Gemini 3 race ahead as US tightens export controls on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs continue rapid iteration on reasoning models while regulatory pressure mounts on compute exports. Funding remains robust with major rounds closing across infrastructure and safety tooling. Prompt injection and multi-agent security emerge as persistent deployment bottlenecks.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4-preview with enhanced chain-of-thought and tool use. Google deployed Gemini 3 across enterprise customers. xAI's Grok-3 and DeepSeek-R2 show competitive performance on coding benchmarks. Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Opus update focuses on constitutional AI refinements.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. Multiple red-team reports highlight successful jailbreaks on frontier APIs. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent and edge deployments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC reports record 3nm wafer demand from AI accelerators. Microsoft and Oracle announce joint 500MW data center campus in Texas. NVIDIA Blackwell supply remains constrained through Q4 2026.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls meaningfully slow Chinese frontier model progress or simply accelerate domestic alternatives?
